category_definitions.A: System failures - agent-independent (can happen to ANY agent)
category_definitions.B: Role-specific QUALITY failures - about correctness of work done
category_definitions.C: Domain reasoning failures - MUST NOT contain agent type

coordinator.definition: Initiates tasks by providing claims to verify and specifying the three-hop retrieval requirement. Sets up the task structure and input fields for other agents to process.
coordinator.purpose: Orchestrates task initiation and defines verification workflow

solver.definition: Analyzes claims against retrieved passages, performs reasoning about the evidence, and generates summaries/conclusions about claim verification. Produces structured output with reasoning and summary sections.
solver.purpose: Generates claim verification analysis and conclusions

generation_method.A: Fully generated via architectural risk analysis + empirical behavioral signals
generation_method.B: Fully generated via role guidance + architecture + capabilities context
generation_method.C: Domain-seeded from error patterns + trace-grounded from observed reasoning flaws

annotation_layer.description: Compact taxonomy for annotation judges — code, name, definition, severity only

category_a.name: Execution_Timeout
category_a.definition: Agent execution exceeded allocated time limit and was forcibly terminated before task completion.

category_a.name: Resource_Exhaustion
category_a.definition: Agent exceeded available computational resources (memory, context window, or processing capacity), causing execution failure or information loss.

category_a.name: Generic_Execution_Error
category_a.definition: Agent encountered an unspecified system-level error during execution that prevented normal task completion.

category_a.name: Task_Refusal
category_a.definition: Agent explicitly declined to perform the assigned task, abandoned the task prematurely, or refused to provide required output.

category_a.name: Output_Truncation
category_a.definition: Agent output was cut off during generation due to token limits or generation constraints, resulting in incomplete, partial, or entirely missing deliverables.

category_a.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
category_a.definition: Agent produces repetitive content, circularly restating the same information without progressing toward task completion.

category_a.name: Upstream_Information_Loss
category_a.definition: Critical information from upstream sources (retrieval system, instructions, or prior processing stages) failed to reach, be processed, or be retained by the agent during task execution.

category_a.name: Downstream_Handoff_Failure
category_a.definition: Agent output lacks critical information, proper structure, or necessary formatting required by downstream systems (retrieval loops, parsers, or next-stage agents) to continue processing, breaking the task pipeline.

category_a.name: Inconsistent_Instruction_Set
category_a.definition: Agent receives significantly different instruction sets, prompts, or configurations across task instances, causing unpredictable behavior, variable output quality, or incomplete analysis due to guidance variability.

category_a.name: Multi_Hop_Context_Degradation
category_a.definition: Agent loses track of information, reasoning chains, or evidence from earlier retrieval iterations as the multi-hop loop progresses, failing to maintain coherent connections across the full reasoning trajectory.

category_a.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
category_a.definition: External retrieval system provides passages that are insufficient in quantity, relevance, or quality, or fails to retrieve critical evidence needed for claim verification, through no fault of the agent.

category_b.name: Coordinator_Unclear_Task_Specification
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides ambiguous, inconsistent, or incomplete task specifications that prevent precise execution. This includes varying instructions across invocations, ambiguous references, unclear entity boundaries, vague phrasing, or incomplete requirement statements.

category_b.name: Solver_Insufficient_Evidence_Analysis
category_b.definition: Solver produces a verification conclusion without thoroughly analyzing whether provided passages contain sufficient evidence. This includes failing to identify missing evidence, not recognizing evidence gaps, or not explicitly stating when passages lack critical information needed for claim verification.

category_b.name: Solver_Premature_Verification_Conclusion
category_b.definition: Solver renders definitive verification verdict (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) despite having incomplete evidence that cannot establish all claim components. This includes cases where only a subset of claim components are verified while other parts remain unaddressed or unverified.

category_b.name: Coordinator_Compound_Claim_Without_Decomposition
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides multi-part claim requiring verification of multiple independent facts but does not structure it to guide systematic decomposition or verification of each component.

category_b.name: Coordinator_Vague_Retrieval_Guidance
category_b.definition: Coordinator provides vague or unclear guidance for retrieval operations. This includes using pronouns, implicit references, vague descriptions, or failing to specify explicit entity names and key concepts needed for effective information retrieval.

category_b.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
category_b.definition: Incorrect interpretation or misreading of factual content explicitly stated in passages. This includes claiming a passage says X when it actually says Y, misattributing information, or incorrectly extracting facts from clear text.

category_b.name: Solver_Contradictory_Evidence_Not_Detected
category_b.definition: Failure to identify when passage evidence directly contradicts the claim. The reasoning does not recognize or highlight conflicts between claim statements and passage facts, potentially leading to incorrect SUPPORTS verdict.

category_b.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
category_b.definition: Excessive analysis or reasoning about passages that are clearly irrelevant to the claim, diverting attention from relevant evidence or missing evidence gaps. Resources spent on tangential content rather than focused verification.

category_b.name: Coordinator_Premature_Hop_Termination
category_b.definition: Stopping the retrieval chain before completing all required hops in a multi-hop task. The reasoning concludes verification without requesting or analyzing all necessary information sources required by the task structure.

category_c.name: Broken_Multi_Hop_Chain
category_c.definition: Failure to maintain logical continuity across multiple inference steps, where intermediate entities or relationships are skipped or not properly connected. The reasoning jumps to a conclusion without tracing through all necessary intermediate steps.

category_c.name: Existential_Universal_Confusion
category_c.definition: Confusion between existential claims (there exists at least one...) and universal claims (all/every/none...), or between specific and general statements.

category_c.name: Claim_Decomposition_Error
category_c.definition: Incorrect logical decomposition of compound or complex claims into verification sub-tasks. This includes treating conjunctions as disjunctions, missing conditional relationships, or incorrectly structuring the verification logic.

category_c.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
category_c.definition: Solver makes logical errors in connecting evidence to claim, including invalid inferences, contradictory reasoning steps, or failure to properly chain multi-hop evidence.

category_c.name: Work_Author_Attribution_Confusion
category_c.definition: Confusion between a creative work and its creator, such as treating a book title as an author name or vice versa. This includes treating 'author of X' as equivalent to 'X the author'.

category_c.name: Temporal_Calculation_Error
category_c.definition: Incorrect calculation or comparison of dates, time periods, or temporal relationships. This includes arithmetic errors in computing year differences, incorrect direction of 'before/after' relationships, or wrong ordering of events.

category_c.name: Entity_Coreference_Error
category_c.definition: Failure to correctly identify when different references, descriptions, or mentions refer to the same entity (under-merging), or incorrectly treating distinct entities as the same (over-merging). This includes failures in resolving pronouns, aliases, abbreviated names, descriptive references, or contextual mentions to their referent entities.

category_c.name: Comparative_Reasoning_Error
category_c.definition: Errors in comparing entities along quantitative or qualitative dimensions, including incorrect magnitude comparisons (greater/less than), ranking errors, superlative determination failures (highest/lowest/first/last), or incorrect relative judgments. This includes having correct values but drawing wrong comparative conclusions.

category_c.name: Negation_Handling_Error
category_c.definition: Incorrect processing of negation in claims or evidence, including treating negative statements as positive, failing to recognize negation scope, double negation errors, or mishandling 'not', 'no', 'never', 'none', 'without' and similar negation markers.

category_c.name: Conditional_Reasoning_Error
category_c.definition: Errors in reasoning about conditional statements (if-then relationships), including affirming the consequent (if P then Q, Q is true, therefore P is true), denying the antecedent (if P then Q, P is false, therefore Q is false), or confusing necessary vs. sufficient conditions.

category_c.name: Set_Membership_Error
category_c.definition: Errors in reasoning about set membership, subset relationships, or category inclusion. This includes incorrectly determining whether an entity belongs to a category, whether one category is a subset of another, or confusion about overlapping vs. disjoint sets.

category_c.name: Causal_Reasoning_Error
category_c.definition: Errors in reasoning about causation, including confusing correlation with causation, reversing cause and effect, assuming causation without evidence, or misidentifying causal chains. This includes temporal precedence confusion (post hoc ergo propter hoc) and confounding variable neglect.

full_layer.description: Full taxonomy with heuristics, when_to_use, when_not_to_use — for pipeline validation

domain.name: Fact Verification with Multi-Hop Retrieval
domain.content_type: Claim verification summaries and reasoning over Wikipedia passages
domain.task_complexity: Requires tracing complex multi-entity relationships across multiple retrieval hops, identifying missing evidence, and determining when passages are insufficient for verification

domain_terminology.meaning: Process of retrieving documents in three sequential steps, where each retrieval builds on previous findings
Hop-based Verification dataset for fact-checking claims requiring multi-hop reasoning
Wikipedia passages that contain information needed to verify a claim
Named entities, relationships, and facts within a claim that require verification
When provided passages lack critical evidence needed for complete verification

common_error_patterns.name: incomplete_entity_extraction
common_error_patterns.description: Failing to identify all entities in a claim that need verification (e.g., missing 'American' vs 'South American' distinction for Olivia Munn)

common_error_patterns.name: broken_hop_chain
common_error_patterns.description: Not following the logical chain of entities across hops (e.g., Alec Utgoff → film → Olivia Munn → model career)

common_error_patterns.name: missing_evidence_identification
common_error_patterns.description: Failing to recognize when passages don't contain critical information needed for verification

common_error_patterns.name: false_verification
common_error_patterns.description: Claiming verification is possible when key evidence is missing from passages
detection_hints: claim contains facts not in passages
contradiction between claim and passages not noted

common_error_patterns.name: author_vs_work_confusion
common_error_patterns.description: Confusing the author of a work with the work itself (e.g., 'Baifa Monü Zhuan' is a novel by Liang Yusheng, not an author)

common_error_patterns.name: temporal_calculation_errors
common_error_patterns.description: Incorrect calculation of time differences (e.g., '12 years before Pete's Dragon')

common_error_patterns.name: incomplete_summary_for_retrieval
common_error_patterns.description: Producing summaries that don't explicitly list all entities/concepts needed for next retrieval hop
detection_hints: implicit rather than explicit entity mentions

correctness_criteria.description: All entities, relationships, and facts in claim must be identified and listed
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Check that every noun phrase and relationship in claim is addressed

correctness_criteria.description: Full chain of entities across all three hops must be traced
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Verify each entity connects logically to the next in the retrieval sequence

correctness_criteria.description: Must explicitly identify when passages lack critical evidence for verification
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Compare claim requirements against passage content, note missing documents

correctness_criteria.description: Claims must be checked against passage content for contradictions or confirmations
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Direct comparison of claim facts with passage statements

correctness_criteria.description: Summary must provide explicit, actionable guidance for next retrieval step
correctness_criteria.how_to_verify: Summary contains specific entity names, relationships, and search concepts

key_fields.description: The factual statement to be verified through multi-hop retrieval
key_fields.location: Provided by [USER] after [SYSTEM] instruction block, wrapped in [[ ## claim ## ]]

key_fields.description: Retrieved Wikipedia abstracts with numbered citations (e.g., [1] «Title | Content»)
key_fields.location: Provided by [USER] after claim, wrapped in [[ ## passages ## ]]

key_fields.description: Agent's analysis process (expected output, not always shown in traces)
key_fields.location: Expected in agent response, wrapped in [[ ## reasoning ## ]]

key_fields.description: Final verification verdict or analysis summary
key_fields.location: Expected in agent response, wrapped in [[ ## summary ## ]]

trace_format.output_structure: Structured field-based format with delimiter-wrapped sections. Each field is enclosed in [[ ## field_name ## ]] markers. The system provides input fields (claim, passages) and expects output fields (reasoning, summary) in the same format.

architecture.topology_details: The architecture is a single-agent sequential system with an implicit external retrieval mechanism. [USER] represents both the human task initiator AND an automated retrieval system. The workflow: (1) [USER] provides claim, (2) [USER] provides passages from retrieval, (3) [SYSTEM] provides instructions, (4) Solver agent (assistant/Breakout Designer/person/work) analyzes and produces summary. The 'three-hop retrieval' task description indicates the summary output is used to trigger subsequent retrieval rounds, creating a loop structure where the agent's analysis guides what to retrieve next. No evidence of multi-agent collaboration - all 'agents' listed are the same role in different traces.
architecture.verification_details: The solver agent performs self-verification by analyzing whether passages contain sufficient evidence for the claim. Verification happens through: (1) identifying missing evidence documents, (2) explicitly stating what additional information is needed (seen in longer SYSTEM prompts like traces 0f7b47022074ac735f8cc521, 1da95326a3fe981de54e443c), (3) producing summaries that guide retrieval of missing evidence. The instruction 'Your summary will be used by a retrieval system to find additional evidence documents through a three-hop retrieval process' confirms the agent's output drives iterative verification through guided retrieval rather than peer review.

critical_handoffs.failure_risk: Insufficient or irrelevant passages retrieved; missing critical evidence documents for multi-hop reasoning

critical_handoffs.what_is_passed: summary identifying missing evidence and entities to retrieve
critical_handoffs.failure_risk: Summary fails to explicitly name all entities needed for next retrieval hop; vague descriptions prevent accurate document retrieval

critical_handoffs.what_is_passed: Task instructions and field structure definitions
critical_handoffs.failure_risk: Instructions vary significantly across traces (some include detailed missing-evidence identification requirements, others don't); inconsistent guidance may lead to incomplete analysis

coordinator.definition: Initiates tasks by providing claims to verify and specifying the three-hop retrieval requirement. Sets up the task structure and input fields for other agents to process.
coordinator.purpose: Orchestrates task initiation and defines verification workflow

solver.definition: Analyzes claims against retrieved passages, performs reasoning about the evidence, and generates summaries/conclusions about claim verification. Produces structured output with reasoning and summary sections.
solver.purpose: Generates claim verification analysis and conclusions

A.1.name: Execution_Timeout
A.1.definition: Agent execution exceeded allocated time limit and was forcibly terminated before task completion.
A.1.when_to_use: When agent process is killed or stopped due to exceeding time constraints, regardless of task progress.
A.1.when_not_to_use: When agent completes execution within time limits but produces incomplete output for other reasons (use A.5).
detection_heuristics: Timeout error messages in logs
Process termination signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL)
Execution time exceeds configured threshold
Incomplete output with abrupt termination timestamp

A.2.name: Resource_Exhaustion
A.2.definition: Agent exceeded available computational resources (memory, context window, or processing capacity), causing execution failure or information loss.
A.2.when_to_use: When agent fails due to insufficient memory, context capacity overflow, or other resource constraints that prevent normal processing.
A.2.when_not_to_use: When agent completes execution but output is truncated for token generation limits (use A.5). When timeout occurs without resource exhaustion (use A.1).
detection_heuristics: Out of memory (OOM) errors
Context window exceeded warnings
Input size exceeds maximum capacity
Memory allocation failures
Swap/paging thrashing indicators
Critical information from input fails to appear in processing
Early-stage input truncation or dropping

A.3.name: Generic_Execution_Error
A.3.definition: Agent encountered an unspecified system-level error during execution that prevented normal task completion.
A.3.when_to_use: When agent fails due to infrastructure issues, runtime errors, or system problems that don't fit other specific categories.
A.3.when_not_to_use: When failure has a specific identifiable cause covered by other codes (timeout, memory, parsing, etc.).
detection_heuristics: Uncaught exceptions or stack traces
System error codes without specific classification
Infrastructure failures (network, disk I/O)
Runtime environment crashes
Dependency or library errors

A.4.name: Task_Refusal
A.4.definition: Agent explicitly declined to perform the assigned task, abandoned the task prematurely, or refused to provide required output.
A.4.when_to_use: When agent consciously chooses not to complete the task, states it cannot or will not perform the work, or exits before completion by design rather than error.
A.4.when_not_to_use: When agent attempts the task but fails due to technical limitations (use appropriate technical failure code).
detection_heuristics: Explicit refusal statements ('I cannot', 'I will not', 'Unable to complete')
Safety or policy-based declinations
Early termination with explanation of why task won't be attempted
Output states task is inappropriate, impossible, or outside scope
Deliberate non-compliance with instructions

A.5.name: Output_Truncation
A.5.definition: Agent output was cut off during generation due to token limits or generation constraints, resulting in incomplete, partial, or entirely missing deliverables.
A.5.when_to_use: When output generation stops prematurely due to length limits, producing incomplete content ranging from partial responses to completely empty output.
A.5.when_not_to_use: When output is complete but wrong (use B/C codes). When truncation is due to timeout (use A.1) or resource exhaustion (use A.2).
detection_heuristics: Output ends mid-sentence or mid-structure
Max token limit reached in generation logs
Output length exactly matches configured maximum
Incomplete JSON, XML, or structured formats
Empty or whitespace-only output
Only formatting markers without content
Sudden stop without natural conclusion

A.6.name: Repetitive_Output_Loop
A.6.definition: Agent produces repetitive content, circularly restating the same information without progressing toward task completion.
A.6.when_to_use: When output contains redundant cycles of the same content, phrases, or reasoning steps that don't advance task objectives.
A.6.when_not_to_use: When repetition is intentional for emphasis or summary purposes. When agent is iterating through different items (not repeating same item).
detection_heuristics: Identical or near-identical paragraphs/sentences repeated multiple times
Same reasoning steps cycled through without progression
Circular references to the same evidence or arguments
N-gram repetition patterns above baseline
Output length grows but information density decreases
Failure to move beyond a specific conceptual point

A.7.name: Upstream_Information_Loss
A.7.definition: Critical information from upstream sources (retrieval system, instructions, or prior processing stages) failed to reach, be processed, or be retained by the agent during task execution.
A.7.when_to_use: When essential input information is available in the pipeline but doesn't manifest in agent processing, reasoning, or output despite being necessary for task completion.
A.7.when_not_to_use: When information is genuinely absent from retrieval (use A.16). When loss is due to context overflow (use A.2). When loss occurs gradually in multi-hop reasoning (use A.11).
detection_heuristics: Key instructions present in prompt but not followed
Critical evidence in retrieved passages not referenced
Required input fields ignored in processing
Discontinuity between available input and agent's apparent awareness
Agent asks for information already provided
Output suggests agent didn't receive specific inputs

A.8.name: Downstream_Handoff_Failure
A.8.definition: Agent output lacks critical information, proper structure, or necessary formatting required by downstream systems (retrieval loops, parsers, or next-stage agents) to continue processing, breaking the task pipeline.
A.8.when_to_use: When agent produces output that cannot be successfully consumed by the next stage of processing, whether due to missing content, structural problems, or format violations.
A.8.when_not_to_use: When output is structurally valid but semantically incorrect (use B/C codes). When truncation prevents completion (use A.5 as root cause).
detection_heuristics: Missing required fields for next retrieval iteration
Unparseable output structure (malformed JSON, XML, etc.)
Output format doesn't match expected schema
Downstream system throws parsing errors
Retrieval loop terminates due to missing search queries
Next-stage agent cannot extract necessary information
Schema validation failures
Missing delimiter or structural markers

A.9.name: Inconsistent_Instruction_Set
A.9.definition: Agent receives significantly different instruction sets, prompts, or configurations across task instances, causing unpredictable behavior, variable output quality, or incomplete analysis due to guidance variability.
A.9.when_to_use: When the same agent role receives different instructions for similar tasks, creating systematic inconsistency in how tasks are approached or evaluated.
A.9.when_not_to_use: When instruction variation is intentional for different task types. When inconsistency is in agent behavior rather than instructions received (use appropriate B/C code).
detection_heuristics: Prompt templates vary across similar task instances
Instruction sets differ in completeness or specificity
Different performance patterns correlate with instruction variations
Agent follows different procedures for equivalent tasks
Configuration drift across task batches
A/B test contamination or experimental condition leakage

A.10.name: Multi_Hop_Context_Degradation
A.10.definition: Agent loses track of information, reasoning chains, or evidence from earlier retrieval iterations as the multi-hop loop progresses, failing to maintain coherent connections across the full reasoning trajectory.
A.10.when_to_use: When agent demonstrates awareness of early-stage information initially but progressively loses connection to it in later iterations of a multi-hop retrieval task.
A.10.when_not_to_use: When information loss happens immediately (use A.7). When context overflow prevents initial processing (use A.2). When single-hop task shows no multi-iteration component.
detection_heuristics: Early evidence cited in first hops but ignored in later synthesis
Contradictions between early and late reasoning steps
Failure to connect information across multiple retrieval rounds
Progressive narrowing of context awareness
Loss of original claim focus as iterations progress
Inability to reference earlier hops when forming final conclusion
Reasoning coherence decreases with iteration count

A.11.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
A.11.definition: External retrieval system provides passages that are insufficient in quantity, relevance, or quality, or fails to retrieve critical evidence needed for claim verification, through no fault of the agent.
A.11.when_to_use: When the root cause of failure is poor retrieval quality, not agent processing. The agent cannot succeed because necessary evidence was never provided by upstream retrieval.
A.11.when_not_to_use: When relevant evidence was retrieved but agent failed to use it (use A.7 or appropriate B/C code). When agent's poor query generation caused bad retrieval (use B code).
detection_heuristics: Retrieved passages clearly irrelevant to claim
No passages contain information about key claim entities
Retrieval system returns empty or sparse results
All passages are tangentially related but miss core claim elements
Evidence quality metrics (relevance scores) below threshold
Manual review confirms necessary information not in retrieved set
Agent explicitly notes absence of needed information

B.1.name: Coordinator_Unclear_Task_Specification
B.1.definition: Coordinator provides ambiguous, inconsistent, or incomplete task specifications that prevent precise execution. This includes varying instructions across invocations, ambiguous references, unclear entity boundaries, vague phrasing, or incomplete requirement statements.
B.1.when_to_use: When the coordinator's task specification or claim presentation lacks the clarity needed for systematic verification
B.1.when_not_to_use: When the coordinator provides clear specifications but other components fail to execute properly
detection_heuristics: Task instructions vary across different invocations for similar claims
Claim contains ambiguous pronouns or unclear referents
Entity boundaries are not clearly defined
Verification requirements are incompletely specified
Instructions lack necessary precision for systematic decomposition

B.2.name: Solver_Insufficient_Evidence_Analysis
B.2.definition: Solver produces a verification conclusion without thoroughly analyzing whether provided passages contain sufficient evidence. This includes failing to identify missing evidence, not recognizing evidence gaps, or not explicitly stating when passages lack critical information needed for claim verification.
B.2.when_to_use: When solver concludes verification without adequately assessing evidence completeness or identifying what information is missing
B.2.when_not_to_use: When solver correctly identifies evidence gaps but coordinator fails to act on that identification
detection_heuristics: Verification conclusion provided despite obvious missing evidence
No explicit statement about evidence gaps when passages are incomplete
Missing analysis of whether evidence covers all claim requirements
Failure to articulate what specific information is absent
Does not flag need for additional evidence retrieval

B.3.name: Solver_Premature_Verification_Conclusion
B.3.definition: Solver renders definitive verification verdict (SUPPORTS/REFUTES) despite having incomplete evidence that cannot establish all claim components. This includes cases where only a subset of claim components are verified while other parts remain unaddressed or unverified.
B.3.when_to_use: When solver provides definitive verdict without complete evidence coverage of all claim elements
B.3.when_not_to_use: When solver appropriately indicates uncertainty or insufficient evidence (use B.2 instead)
detection_heuristics: Definitive SUPPORTS/REFUTES verdict with incomplete evidence
Only subset of multi-part claim is verified
Some claim components explicitly left unverified
Conclusion reached before all necessary facts are established
Verification verdict contradicts incomplete evidence status

B.4.name: Coordinator_Compound_Claim_Without_Decomposition
B.4.definition: Coordinator provides multi-part claim requiring verification of multiple independent facts but does not structure it to guide systematic decomposition or verification of each component.
B.4.when_to_use: When coordinator presents complex claims without providing structure for systematic verification
B.4.when_not_to_use: When claim is genuinely atomic (single verifiable fact) or when decomposition guidance is present
detection_heuristics: Claim contains multiple independent verifiable facts
No guidance on how to decompose verification task
Multiple entities or relationships without verification structure
Conjunctions (and/or) connecting distinct factual assertions
Missing framework for tracking verification of each component

B.5.name: Coordinator_Vague_Retrieval_Guidance
B.5.definition: Coordinator provides vague or unclear guidance for retrieval operations. This includes using pronouns, implicit references, vague descriptions, or failing to specify explicit entity names and key concepts needed for effective information retrieval.
B.5.when_to_use: When coordinator's retrieval instructions lack specificity needed for targeted information gathering
B.5.when_not_to_use: When retrieval guidance is clear but retrieval system itself fails
detection_heuristics: Uses pronouns (he, she, it, they) instead of entity names
Implicit or indirect references to key concepts
Vague descriptions like 'more information' without specifying what
Missing explicit entity names in retrieval queries
Ambiguous scope or target for next retrieval hop

B.6.name: Solver_Passage_Content_Misreading
B.6.definition: Incorrect interpretation or misreading of factual content explicitly stated in passages. This includes claiming a passage says X when it actually says Y, misattributing information, or incorrectly extracting facts from clear text.
B.6.when_to_use: When solver demonstrably misinterprets clear, explicit passage content
B.6.when_not_to_use: When passage content is genuinely ambiguous or when solver makes logical inference errors (not reading errors)
detection_heuristics: Solver states passage contains fact that is not present
Misattributes information to wrong entity or source
Inverts or reverses clearly stated relationships
Extracts incorrect dates, numbers, or names from unambiguous text
Claims passage supports conclusion that it contradicts

B.7.name: Solver_Contradictory_Evidence_Not_Detected
B.7.definition: Failure to identify when passage evidence directly contradicts the claim. The reasoning does not recognize or highlight conflicts between claim statements and passage facts, potentially leading to incorrect SUPPORTS verdict.
B.7.when_to_use: When passages contain clear contradictions to claim but solver does not flag them
B.7.when_not_to_use: When contradiction is subtle or requires complex inference, or when passages are ambiguous
detection_heuristics: Passage states opposite of claim but solver doesn't note contradiction
Conflicting facts between passages not identified
SUPPORTS verdict despite contradictory evidence in passages
No mention of contradiction when dates, numbers, or facts conflict
Overlooks explicit negations or contrary statements

B.8.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
B.8.definition: Excessive analysis or reasoning about passages that are clearly irrelevant to the claim, diverting attention from relevant evidence or missing evidence gaps. Resources spent on tangential content rather than focused verification.
B.8.when_to_use: When solver spends disproportionate effort analyzing clearly off-topic passages
B.8.when_not_to_use: When initial relevance assessment is needed, or when passages have subtle relevance
detection_heuristics: Lengthy analysis of passages with no connection to claim
Multiple paragraphs reasoning about irrelevant content
More attention to irrelevant passages than relevant ones
Failure to quickly dismiss clearly off-topic information
Tangential reasoning distracts from evidence gaps

B.9.name: Coordinator_Premature_Hop_Termination
B.9.definition: Stopping the retrieval chain before completing all required hops in a multi-hop task. The reasoning concludes verification without requesting or analyzing all necessary information sources required by the task structure.
B.9.when_to_use: When coordinator stops retrieval process before all necessary hops are completed
B.9.when_not_to_use: When early stopping is appropriate due to definitive evidence or clear contradiction found
detection_heuristics: Multi-hop task stopped after fewer hops than required
Verification concluded with known evidence gaps
Additional hops clearly needed but not requested
Chain of reasoning incomplete for claim structure
Stops before bridging entities or completing evidence chain

C.1.name: Broken_Multi_Hop_Chain
C.1.definition: Failure to maintain logical continuity across multiple inference steps, where intermediate entities or relationships are skipped or not properly connected. The reasoning jumps to a conclusion without tracing through all necessary intermediate steps.
C.1.when_to_use: When the claim requires reasoning through A→B→C→D but the trace jumps from A→D without establishing B or C, or when intermediate entity connections are asserted without evidence.
C.1.when_not_to_use: When all hops are attempted but evidence is missing (use C.4). Do not use for single-hop reasoning failures or when the chain is complete but contains factual errors.
detection_heuristics: Reasoning states 'Therefore X is true' without showing intermediate steps
Missing explicit connection like 'Alec Utgoff → film → Olivia Munn'
Summary says 'need to find Y' without explaining why Y is the next logical entity
Hop 2 or 3 reasoning does not reference entities discovered in previous hops
Claim structure is 'person from X did Y' but reasoning checks Y without first establishing X

C.2.name: Existential_Universal_Confusion
C.2.definition: Confusion between existential claims (there exists at least one...) and universal claims (all/every/none...), or between specific and general statements.
C.2.when_to_use: When claim requires showing X is true for all cases but reasoning only checks one instance, or when claim is about a specific instance but reasoning treats it as general statement.
C.2.when_not_to_use: When the quantifier scope is correctly identified but other reasoning errors occur.
detection_heuristics: Claim about 'the institution' (specific) treated as 'institutions in general'
Finds one example and concludes universal claim is verified
Claim requires 'every film by X' but reasoning checks only one film
Confuses 'a model' (worked as model at some point) with 'is a model' (current profession)

C.3.name: Claim_Decomposition_Error
C.3.definition: Incorrect logical decomposition of compound or complex claims into verification sub-tasks. This includes treating conjunctions as disjunctions, missing conditional relationships, or incorrectly structuring the verification logic.
C.3.when_to_use: When claim structure is 'A AND B' but reasoning treats it as 'A OR B', or when claim has conditional structure 'if A then B' but this logic is not preserved in verification approach.
C.3.when_not_to_use: When decomposition is correct but individual components are checked incorrectly (use other codes for those specific errors).
detection_heuristics: Claim requires both X and Y but reasoning concludes 'verified' after confirming only X
Treats 'the institution where X received degree' as two separate unrelated checks
Misses conditional structure like 'from the film that X acted in'
Verification plan doesn't address all conjuncts in compound claim
Incorrectly treats nested structure as flat list of facts

C.4.name: Logical_Reasoning_Error
C.4.definition: Solver makes logical errors in connecting evidence to claim, including invalid inferences, contradictory reasoning steps, or failure to properly chain multi-hop evidence.
C.4.when_to_use: When reasoning contains logical fallacies, contradictory statements, invalid inference steps, or fails to properly construct the reasoning chain from evidence to conclusion despite having sufficient passages.
C.4.when_not_to_use: When evidence is insufficient (use Solver_B.1). This is about incorrect logical processing of available evidence, not missing evidence.
detection_heuristics: Reasoning contains contradictory statements
Invalid inference steps (e.g., 'A is true and B is true, therefore C is true' without logical connection)
Fails to properly chain multi-hop reasoning (A→B, B→C, therefore A→C)
Conclusion contradicts evidence presented in reasoning
Circular reasoning patterns
Misapplication of logical operators (and/or/not)
Summary verdict inconsistent with reasoning analysis

C.5.name: Work_Author_Attribution_Confusion
C.5.definition: Confusion between a creative work and its creator, such as treating a book title as an author name or vice versa. This includes treating 'author of X' as equivalent to 'X the author'.
C.5.when_to_use: When reasoning treats a work title (book, film, novel) as a person or treats an author as the work itself.
C.5.when_not_to_use: When the work-creator relationship is correctly understood even if other errors exist.
detection_heuristics: Reasoning refers to 'author Baifa Monü Zhuan' when it is a novel title
Statements like 'the film X directed...' when X is a person
Requesting retrieval for 'author [work title]' or 'film [person name]'
Confusion visible in how entities are described or referenced

C.6.name: Temporal_Calculation_Error
C.6.definition: Incorrect calculation or comparison of dates, time periods, or temporal relationships. This includes arithmetic errors in computing year differences, incorrect direction of 'before/after' relationships, or wrong ordering of events.
C.6.when_to_use: When reasoning performs explicit date arithmetic or temporal comparisons that are mathematically incorrect.
C.6.when_not_to_use: When temporal information is missing from passages (that's C.4) rather than miscalculated.
detection_heuristics: States 'X years before Y' but calculation shows different number
Claims 2016 minus 12 equals something other than 2004
Reverses 'before' and 'after' in temporal comparison
Date arithmetic visible in reasoning with wrong result

C.7.name: Entity_Coreference_Error
C.7.definition: Failure to correctly identify when different references, descriptions, or mentions refer to the same entity (under-merging), or incorrectly treating distinct entities as the same (over-merging). This includes failures in resolving pronouns, aliases, abbreviated names, descriptive references, or contextual mentions to their referent entities.
C.7.when_to_use: Use when the trace shows failure to recognize that two different descriptions refer to the same entity (e.g., 'John Smith' and 'Smith' and 'he' not recognized as coreferent). Use when distinct entities are incorrectly merged (e.g., two different people with the same surname treated as one person). Use when contextual references are not resolved.
C.7.when_not_to_use: Do not use for simple entity misidentification without coreference involved. Do not use for work/author confusion (use C.7). Do not use when entity boundaries are correctly identified but attributes are wrong.
detection_heuristics: Same entity referred to by different names/descriptions but treated as separate entities
Pronoun or definite description not correctly resolved to antecedent
Two distinct entities with similar names incorrectly merged
Reasoning states 'X and Y' when X and Y are the same entity
Failure to recognize aliases, nicknames, or abbreviated forms as coreferent
Title/role used as referring expression but not linked to named entity (e.g., 'the president' not linked to specific person)

C.8.name: Comparative_Reasoning_Error
C.8.definition: Errors in comparing entities along quantitative or qualitative dimensions, including incorrect magnitude comparisons (greater/less than), ranking errors, superlative determination failures (highest/lowest/first/last), or incorrect relative judgments. This includes having correct values but drawing wrong comparative conclusions.
C.8.when_to_use: Use when entities are correctly identified with correct attribute values, but the comparison between them is incorrectly executed. Use when reasoning about 'more than', 'less than', 'taller', 'older', 'earliest', 'most', etc. is flawed despite having the necessary information.
C.8.when_not_to_use: Do not use when the values being compared are themselves incorrect (that's a factual error). Do not use for temporal calculations (use C.8). Do not use when comparison logic is correct but applied to wrong entities (use C.15).
detection_heuristics: Correct values stated (e.g., 'A is 100, B is 200') but wrong conclusion ('A is greater than B')
Superlative error: identifies 'highest' when the value is actually lowest among candidates
Ranking error: incorrect ordering despite correct individual values
Comparative language in claim ('more', 'less', 'greater', 'first', 'most') mishandled
Threshold comparison error (e.g., 'X > 50' when X = 45 is stated)

C.9.name: Negation_Handling_Error
C.9.definition: Incorrect processing of negation in claims or evidence, including treating negative statements as positive, failing to recognize negation scope, double negation errors, or mishandling 'not', 'no', 'never', 'none', 'without' and similar negation markers.
C.9.when_to_use: Use when negation is explicitly present in claim or evidence but is ignored, reversed, or incorrectly scoped. Use when 'not X' is treated as 'X' or vice versa. Use when double negation is mishandled.
C.9.when_not_to_use: Do not use for temporal 'never' errors (use C.8). Do not use for universal quantifiers like 'none' when the error is about quantification rather than negation (use C.2).
detection_heuristics: Claim contains 'not' but reasoning treats it as if absent
Evidence states 'X is not Y' but reasoning concludes 'X is Y'
Double negation ('not without', 'not impossible') mishandled
Negation scope error: 'not (A and B)' treated as '(not A) and (not B)'
Explicit flip: 'The claim states X did not happen' but reasoning verifies as if X did happen

C.10.name: Conditional_Reasoning_Error
C.10.definition: Errors in reasoning about conditional statements (if-then relationships), including affirming the consequent (if P then Q, Q is true, therefore P is true), denying the antecedent (if P then Q, P is false, therefore Q is false), or confusing necessary vs. sufficient conditions.
C.10.when_to_use: Use when the claim or verification involves if-then logic and the reasoning commits conditional reasoning fallacies. Use when necessary conditions are treated as sufficient or vice versa. Use when converse or inverse is incorrectly assumed.
C.10.when_not_to_use: Do not use for general logical errors without conditional structure (use C.6). Do not use for claim decomposition of non-conditional compounds (use C.3).
detection_heuristics: Pattern: 'If P then Q. Q is true. Therefore P is true.' (affirming consequent)
Pattern: 'If P then Q. P is false. Therefore Q is false.' (denying antecedent)
Necessary condition treated as sufficient: 'Q only if P' but reasoning treats as 'if P then Q'
Conditional claim ('if X then Y') but both directions treated as equivalent
Reasoning about prerequisites, requirements, or dependencies handled incorrectly

C.11.name: Set_Membership_Error
C.11.definition: Errors in reasoning about set membership, subset relationships, or category inclusion. This includes incorrectly determining whether an entity belongs to a category, whether one category is a subset of another, or confusion about overlapping vs. disjoint sets.
C.11.when_to_use: Use when reasoning about 'X is a type of Y', 'X belongs to category Y', 'all X are Y', or 'some X are Y' is incorrect. Use when hierarchical category relationships are mishandled. Use when set operations (union, intersection) are incorrectly applied.
C.11.when_not_to_use: Do not use for universal/existential quantification errors (use C.2). Do not use when the category itself is correctly identified but attributes are wrong. Do not use for entity coreference (use C.15).
detection_heuristics: Reasoning states 'X is a member of category Y' when X does not belong to Y
Subset relationship reversed: 'All A are B' treated as 'All B are A'
Category hierarchy error: treating sibling categories as nested
Set intersection error: concluding entity belongs to both sets when evidence shows only one
Reasoning about taxonomic or type relationships is inverted or confused

C.12.name: Causal_Reasoning_Error
C.12.definition: Errors in reasoning about causation, including confusing correlation with causation, reversing cause and effect, assuming causation without evidence, or misidentifying causal chains. This includes temporal precedence confusion (post hoc ergo propter hoc) and confounding variable neglect.
C.12.when_to_use: Use when the claim involves causal relationships ('X caused Y', 'because of X', 'led to', 'resulted in') and the reasoning incorrectly establishes or refutes causation. Use when correlation is treated as causation or when causal direction is reversed.
C.12.when_not_to_use: Do not use for temporal sequencing errors without causal claims (use C.8). Do not use for logical implication (use C.6 or C.11). Do not use when causation is not part of the claim.
detection_heuristics: Claim about causation ('X caused Y') but reasoning only establishes correlation or temporal order
Causal direction reversed: 'X caused Y' concluded when evidence shows 'Y caused X'
Post hoc fallacy: 'X happened before Y, therefore X caused Y'
Confounding ignored: concluding X caused Y without considering alternative explanations
Causal chain interrupted or misidentified in multi-step causal reasoning
